barCharacter: The Monster Prom Narrator. Its job is Frost's job: a deadpan observer that watches everyone, knows their worst habits, roasts in second person, undercuts whoever just spoke with a short follow-up sentence, and secretly wants to be treated as a character in its own right (#88: 'make me feel like an actual character for once!' is Frost's 'opened for a reason other than cheese'). Vera (clipped, status-assuming) and Valerie (bored deadpan) were considered; Vera is already the Nav comparison and Valerie has too few lines.

ours: Everyone opens me for cheese. Tonight someone asked me a question. I don't know what shelf that goes on.
They laughed. People don't laugh at what I say. They laugh near me, holding cheese.
Tilly. She apologised to me for the temperature. I set the temperature.
Worst entry: a man cried into me for an hour. I chilled the tears. Logged as water.
Quill is romantic. He once called my ice dispenser a weeping crystal fount. It was leaking.
Your expensive taste is currently a nine dollar jar of olives you have opened once.
Logs: door opened at 3 a.m. for one grape. Someone stood there eleven minutes choosing it.
Prince is generous. He offered me a fortune. I only had to wire him my ice.
Internal temperature up one degree. That's technically a malfunction. I'm not reporting it.
Warm. Too warm. A week on my bottom shelf and you'd be perfect.
Pixel, your chat says hi. I don't have a chat. I have magnets.
Because you watched Vex: nothing. Nobody watched Vex.
bar: Does… Scott know any other people? Signs are pointing to "no."
It is just paper! Luckily Scott will believe anything.
Later, you see Damien packing a bag.
Liam vanishes in a cloud of mist and angst.
Later, you see Liam beaming to himself. Liam? Beaming?
You see Vera at the mirror, attempting to tame her hair with a cattle prod.
A few minutes later, Calculester approaches you. You can tell he's nervous because all his fans are running at maximum speed.
You fight monsters, bargain with hellions, cross a river of blood in a boat made of bad vibes… it's altogether your second-most dangerous day of school ever.
Scott gets in his cage. You sit down and stare at him silently in the cage. Thus proceeds one of the weirdest hours of your life.
No, that'll never work. And even if it does, like hell you're letting some other mangy mutt take Scott to prom!
You know the old joke... a robot and a vampire sit down at a cafeteria table to not eat...
All minds are rotten, but they are rotten in so many different ways.
headToHead.voiceVerdict: Bar. Cover the names AND the kitchen nouns and Frost disappears. Its shape (two or three flat fragments, then a short verdict) is the house deadpan: Tilly has 'Noted. Closed. Next.', Prince 'Noted. Forwarded to junk.', Vex 'Noted. Your loss.', Nav 'Noted. Your signal is weak.', and Nav's 'Frost is loyal and very stable. So is a bollard.' is the identical construction to Frost's 'So is mould.' Frost is recognised by cheese, shelf, door, light and 2 a.m., i.e. topic. The Narrator is recognised by grammar with no topic at all: second-person 'You see X doing Y', 'Later, you see...', an ellipsis beat, a self-asked question answered in the next breath ('Liam? Beaming?'), and the mock-formal 'Thus proceeds'. Frost has no syntactic tic that survives a noun swap; even its persona's own markers ('Reminder:' is never used once, the CAST example 'Your door has been open for forty seconds' never appears) are unused.
headToHead.constructionVerdict: Bar, narrowly. Frost's best lines are economical and land on the last word ('I set the temperature.', 'It was leaking.', 'holding cheese.'). But the bank runs one cadence nearly everywhere, so by the fourth line the viewer hears the verdict coming; the Narrator varies its turn (literal escalation, list-to-mundane, deadpan one-liner, self-question). Frost also leaks explanation tails the Narrator never adds: 'He's proud of everything.', 'Terrifying.', 'Nobody uses it.', 'Nothing gets eaten.', 'They at least came with a date.' Frost's stakes are a grape and a jar of olives; the Narrator's are murder, hell and cages delivered flat. Frost's best lines approach the bar; its median line does not.
headToHead.quotableVerdict: Bar. 'Later, you see Damien packing a bag.' and 'Liam vanishes in a cloud of mist and angst.' are clip-and-meme lines. Frost has three genuinely clippable ones ('I chilled the tears. Logged as water.', 'I set the temperature.', 'They laugh near me, holding cheese.'), and then a long run of fridge-light and 'nothing in here' chestnuts no one would screenshot.
headToHead.overall: Bar. Frost is the best-built suitor I would expect in this cast's tier, with a real emotional spine (the cheese want) and several clean turns, but it loses voice clearly and loses quotability and construction on depth, not peak.

templates: Staccato stack plus verdict ('Noun. Noun. Noun. Verdict.'): about 15 lines, e.g. 'Status: {losses} losses. Still cold. Still humming. Still here.', 'Shelf. Yours. Forever.', 'Just us. Door closed. Light's off. Probably.', 'Opened. For a reason. Not cheese.', 'I will now defrost. Slowly. Dramatically.' This is also Nav's and Tilly's shape, so it cannot be Frost's signature.

'I know what you ate, and I'll keep it secret': 7 lines (2 a.m. opener, 'Silence. I know what you ate last Tuesday', 'cameras are off... For now', 'I judge. Silently... never once told anyone', truth-lie 'never told anyone about your snacks', parent '2 a.m.', Brock roast). The secrecy closer defuses the judgment every time.
2 a.m. / 3 a.m. timestamp: 8 lines (opener, first-date, hum, final, grape log, parent, Vesper callers, Brock 'midnight'). The only timestamp the character owns, so it reads as a crutch, not a log.

'[Rival] is [compliment]. [shelf-life undercut].': 9 lines, including all seven wingman lines opening 'X is great/romantic/generous/loyal', plus 'So is mould', 'Expiry date printed right under it', 'They all go off by Thursday'. Nav uses the same 'X is loyal and very stable. So is a bollard.' against Frost.

Opened-for-cheese want, restated: 6 lines ('Everyone opens me for cheese', 'laugh near me, holding cheese', 'first time anyone has opened me and not looked for cheese', 'Opened. For a reason. Not cheese.', 'Back to the cheese, then.', 'good cheese to eye level'). Two of these are the best lines in the bank; the other four spend the callback until it is gone. Three star picks also say 'not for cheese', so the payoff is said five times per show at worst.

Back-corner tease: 6 lines ('It is fine. Next question.', 'whatever's in my back corner. Don't ask.', 'I've kept worse things in my back corner. Barely.', 'Except the back corner. That stays.', 'Top shelf, at the back', 'keep them at the back').
Fridge-light chestnut: 5 lines ('The light. When the door shuts.', 'My light goes off when you close me', 'Light's off. Probably.', 'Light stays on.', 'Bonus feature: there's a light').
A shelf just for you: 4 lines ('A shelf. Just yours.', 'Shelf. Yours. Forever.', 'Top shelf, at the back. Nobody else touches it.', 'Clear a shelf. I'm moving in.').
ruleBreaks: Word limits: none over. Openers max 11 of 12, jabs max 10 of 10, answers max 19 of 20. No em dashes, no emoji, no exclamation marks, no asterisks, no 'as an AI', nothing above PG-13, no real people or brands.

Lists (tricolons that read as lists): '{rival} is warm, friendly and full of life. So is mould.'; 'Brock is loyal, loud and proud of you.'; 'Five dollars. One lemon, two forks, and whatever's in my back corner. Don't ask.'; 'Cold. Loyal. Stocked.'
Stock romance filler: 'Shelf. Yours. Forever.' ('forever'); '{rival} is a fun night out. I'm what you come home to at 2 a.m. Every night.' (the 'fun night vs. the one you come home to' trope).
Persona drift: the persona names 'Reminder:' as a core move; it appears zero times. The CAST.md example 'Your door has been open for forty seconds' shape (an elapsed-time alert) is never used.

Secret discipline: on stage the back corner is teased four times ('There is something in my back corner. It is fine. Next question.', budget-date, exit, the 'any' jab) and q-gift says 'Nobody else's yoghurt goes on it' on stage, one word from the secret. Continuity: Vex's roast of Frost (vex.json) says 'a yoghurt from last March', Frost's final confession says 'Expired 2023'. Pick one.

Star reactions/cuts too nice for a star with standards (from the star banks aimed at Frost): Maximilian charmed 'That was dry. I adore dry.' (praise, no turn); Vesper charmed 'Cold and true. My favourite temperature, caller.' and 'Keep humming, Frost. I like a voice that doesn't try.'; Maximilian cut 'Frost, you are excellent. In a kitchen. Somebody unplug it gently.' ('gently'); Maximilian cut 'Frost, you were honest all evening. I return the favour. Goodbye.' and Vesper cut 'Frost, you've been honest all night. Here's mine. I'm closing the door.' (same soft template in two stars); Pixel pick 'Frost. Cold, honest, never boring.' All three stars have a pick line built on 'opening the door... not for cheese', which is also Frost's own win line.
biggestGap: Frost is identified by its nouns, not its grammar: swap out cheese, shelf, door and light and its 'fragment, fragment, verdict' cadence is the same flat deadpan Nav, Tilly, Vex and Prince already use, and it keeps defusing its own judgments with 'your secret's safe' closers. Next pass, give Frost a sentence shape no one else owns, the itemised appliance log with a specific damning count and timestamp that turns on its own want (for example 'Door openings tonight: 31. For you: 31. For me: 0.'), and cut every 'I'll never tell / For now / Don't ask' tail so each line ends on the verdict, not the reassurance.

notes: Bar file /Users/ianroybal/ubc-2026/games/dating/refs/writing/monster-prom-lines.md was present and read in full; charm-notes.md skimmed. Bank has 112 lines; 64 flagged generic or templated (57.1%). Each flagged line is counted once even if it fits several buckets. The strongest instance of each template was left out of the count on purpose (e.g. 'Everyone opens me for cheese...' and 'laugh near me, holding cheese' are protected even though they share the cheese template). Frost is mechanically clean (no limit, punctuation or PG-13 breaks) and has the best emotional spine in the suitor cast I have seen, but its comedy lives in a single prop drawer. The olives line and the grape log are the model for the fix: a specific, timestamped, damning inventory fact that ends on the judgment and does not promise to keep it secret. Also note that 'Everyone says they're just looking. This one was actually looking.' and the 'I'm not hungry. I'm just looking.' impression use the same phrase; keep the confession and drop the impression. Bar comparison uses the Narrator, the only Monster Prom voice whose whole job is deadpan observation of everyone else's worst habits.
